Tate brothers’ US extradition case a ‘step towards accountability,’ says independent expert UN Photo/Rick Bajornas Reem Alsalem, Special Rapporteur on violence against women and girls, its causes and consequences Wednesday, August 05, 2026 UN News An independent UN human rights expert has welcomed ongoing proceedings in the United States to extradite “manosphere” bloggers Andrew and Tristan Tate to the United Kingdom, calling the case an important step towards accountability for serious allegations of violence against women and girls. The proceedings “ offer renewed hope that justice may finally be achieved through effective international cooperation ,” said Reem Alsalem, Special Rapporteur on violence against women and girls. She noted that the action taken comes after years in which women’s testimonies and experiences had been ignored or dismissed by law enforcement and prosecutorial authorities. Call for justice “ Given the scale of the alleged offences, and the Tate brothers’ global influence in promoting misogyny and harmful models of masculinity, it is urgent and imperative that they face justice ,” she said. The Tate brothers – dual British-US nationals and former professional kickboxers-turned-social media influencers – were arrested in Miami, Florida, on 18 July following an extradition request from the UK. They remain in custody in the US while challenging the extradition request, where they face 59 criminal charges, including rape, sexual assault, facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation, assault, and offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography . Separate criminal proceedings remain ongoing in Romania concerning allegations including human trafficking, including the trafficking of minors. ‘No one should be above the law’ Ms. Alsalem urged the Governments of Romania, the UK and the US to ensure that the Tate brothers face justice. " All too often, perpetrators of violence against women exploit delays, fragmented jurisdictional responses and their wealth, power or influential public profile to evade accountability ,” she said, stressing that “no one should be above the law, regardless of their status, influence or international reach.” She also called for the justice process to be expanded to include those that aided, abetted and profited from the Tate brothers’ criminal enterprise of grooming, exploiting and abusing women and girls, rather than focusing only on individual criminal responsibility. On 4 March, Ms. Alsalem transmitted information she had received to the Governments of Romania and the United Kingdom – with copies to the United States – regarding the poor handling of allegations of rape, strangulation, intimidation and retaliation made by a woman who alleged that she had been sexually assaulted by Andrew Tate in Romania in 2018. Special Rapporteurs are independent experts appointed by the Human Rights Council in Geneva. They are not United Nations staff and do not receive a salary for their work. © UN News (2026) — All Rights Reserved . Original source: UN News Where next? https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/vik.text: The Budapest Times Viktor Orbán’s brother jailed pending trial over people-smuggling ring The Buda Central District Court ordered the one-month pre-trial detention of Áron Orbán and his partner on Wednesday. One suspect was placed under criminal supervision, while another may defend themselves at liberty. Áron Orbán, the brother of former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, and his associates are suspected of people smuggling carried out in an organised manner and as part of a criminal conspiracy. Gergő Bozó, spokesperson for the Budapest Metropolitan Court, said following the decision that the court had no doubt regarding any of the suspects as to the existence of reasonable suspicion. In the case of the three suspects subject to coercive measures, the court concluded that there was a risk of flight or concealment. In this context, it assessed the particularly serious nature of the offence under investigation, the potential severity of the sentence in the event of conviction, and the suspects’ extensive network of foreign connections, the spokesperson said. In the case of the two detained suspects, there is also a risk of influencing the evidentiary proceedings — specifically, the risk of influencing further witness testimony. For this reason, the court found no basis, at the current stage of the proceedings, for ordering a measure less restrictive than detention in their cases. According to the court’s assessment, the procedural presence of the third suspect can be ensured through the application of criminal supervision. The suspect is required to wear a tracking device and may not leave the country for four months, Gergő Bozó said. The spokesperson noted that the court’s ruling is not final. The Budapest Chief Prosecution Office filed a motion for the pre-trial detention of all four suspects. In its submission, the office stated that the criminal offence attributed to the suspects is of significant objective gravity, and that the sentence applicable upon conviction — imprisonment of five to ten years — is severe. Furthermore, based on the available data, the suspects have an extensive network of foreign contacts. In light of all this, it can be reasonably concluded that the presence of the accused in the criminal proceedings can only be secured through their detention, the prosecution wrote. The substance of the suspicion is that Áron Orbán, his partner, and two associates provided assistance to at least one hundred Vietnamese nationals in illegally crossing the state border on a commercial basis and for financial gain from 2022 onwards. Members of the group assisted in obtaining visas at Hungarian diplomatic missions abroad, for which they charged a recruitment fee per person. The alleged perpetrators shared the proceeds among themselves. In some of the visa applications, short-term training in Hungary was listed as the purpose of entry, though the majority of those involved did not participate in any such training. The National Investigation Office, together with the National Asset Recovery and Asset Protection Office (NVVH), carried out searches on Monday morning at multiple locations in Budapest, Fót, and Dunakeszi. In addition to taking the suspects into custody, officers seized all equipment, documents, and electronic data that may serve as evidence in the human smuggling and corruption case.
